answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks via acoustic bathymetry across a monitored lagoon. Each node emits a sonar pulse and records the seabed echo, calibrating transit times against water ripple patterns to prove its physical location. Because aquatic sound propagation cannot be emulated in software, an attacker must deploy discrete transducer hardware per identity. However, water temperature fluctuations alter acoustic velocity, occasionally causing false rejections.
